skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples, API key placeholders, local URLs, or Markdown fences rather than active malicious code. The real concerns are examples that send local source content to Gemini and workflow guidance that can delegate user data or run full-auto provider commands without a hard consent gate.

remediation.issue: External provider prompts can include local source files.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit user consent step before sending files or proprietary context to Gemini, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, or other cloud providers.

remediation.issue: Codex full-auto mode can approve actions without review.
remediation.suggestion: Require a sandbox flag and explicit user confirmation before recommending full-auto execution.

remediation.issue: Shell examples inline files into prompts.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer named file attachments or narrowly scoped file lists, and warn users before expanding entire directories into provider prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Consent Gate Before External Delegation
semantic_findings.description: The workflow warns against sending sensitive data without consent, but the execution steps do not require explicit user approval before delegating context to cloud providers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The relevant lines explicitly discuss provider delegation and sensitive data, but the checklist only confirms authentication before execution. This makes the risk contextual rather than evidence of malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Auto-Approval Execution Mode
semantic_findings.description: The Codex cookbook recommends full-auto execution, which can approve provider actions without step-by-step review if used outside a strong sandbox.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command and warning are present in the same section, and the sample full-auto command does not include an explicit sandbox flag. The documented warning reduces but does not remove the operational risk.

content.user_title: Route Tasks Across AI Coding Agents
content.value_statement: Teams waste time deciding which AI provider should handle each task. This skill routes work across Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and Ollama with provider guidance.
actual_capabilities: Routes tasks with a provider decision tree and capability matrix.
Provides cookbook commands for Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and Ollama.
Documents authentication prerequisites for subscription and API key workflows.
Explains when to use local Ollama for private or offline tasks.
Defines parallel execution patterns, timeout handling, and result collection.
Guides model tier selection for speed, cost, and task difficulty.
limitations: Requires provider CLIs, accounts, or local models to be installed separately.
Does not automatically verify current model names without the model-discovery skill.
Delegated work may lose conversation history unless context is copied into the task.
Cloud providers may receive prompts and files unless the user limits shared context.

use_cases.title: Route Coding Work
use_cases.description: Choose the best AI provider for code generation, refactoring, testing, or architecture work.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Research Agents
use_cases.description: Run parallel research tasks with different providers, then collect and summarize the results.

use_cases.title: Protect Sensitive Context
use_cases.description: Select local Ollama or keep work in Claude when privacy or conversation history matters.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Provider
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner routing for a single task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-orchestration to choose the best provider for this task: [describe task]. Explain the provider choice and fallback.

prompt_templates.title: Delegate a Coding Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Run one focused implementation or review task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this coding task to the right provider, check prerequisites, and summarize the result: [task details]. Avoid sharing sensitive files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Parallel Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Split a research problem across several agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel agent plan for this research question: [question]. Assign providers, timeouts, expected outputs, and synthesis steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Fallback Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced orchestration with cost and privacy constraints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a provider routing and fallback strategy for [workflow]. Include model tiers, cost checks, privacy rules, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Route a large codebase analysis task with current documentation research.
output_examples.output: Recommended provider: Gemini for large context and web grounding. Fallback: Claude for synthesis if search is not required.

output_examples.input: Plan a private review of sensitive source files.
output_examples.output: Recommended provider: Ollama for local processing. Keep cloud providers out unless the user approves a reduced, sanitized excerpt.

output_examples.input: Coordinate six quick research checks and one final summary.
output_examples.output: Use fast worker agents for independent checks, then use a stronger synthesis model for the final summary and confidence notes.

best_practices: Confirm provider availability and cost before delegation.
Ask before sending proprietary or sensitive content to cloud providers.
Use focused task prompts with clear expected outputs and fallback rules.
anti_patterns: Delegating tasks that require current conversation history.
Running full-auto provider commands outside a sandbox.
Sending whole repositories to external providers when a focused file set is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill run agents automatically?
faq.answer: It provides routing guidance and cookbook commands. Actual execution depends on the available tools and user approval.

faq.question: Which providers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and local Ollama workflows.

faq.question: Can it handle private code?
faq.answer: Yes, but use local Ollama or keep the task in Claude unless the user approves external sharing.

faq.question: Does it choose current model names?
faq.answer: It points to a model-discovery skill for current names because model versions change often.

faq.question: What makes it useful for parallel work?
faq.answer: It shows how to launch multiple agents together, tag each agent, collect results, and handle timeouts.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install and authenticate the provider CLIs you plan to use, or run Ollama locally with pulled models.
